value:
Bustos began as a barrio of Baliuag. In 1862 a boat carrying parents, children and godparents to a baptism in Baliuag overturned on the Angat River, and the grief that followed led the people to ask for their own town and parish. Bustos separated from Baliuag on 29 April 1867, was returned to it during the American period, and became a municipality again on 1 January 1916; its first municipal hall opened in 1917 with Leon Prado as mayor.

The park also remembers the town's role in World War II. The Bulacan Military Area, formed on 3 July 1942, made Bustos the headquarters of the province's guerrillas under Bustos-born Capt. (later General) Alejo Santos. A historical marker for Santos was unveiled here in 2022, and the BMA grounds host the Minasa Festival every January.

value:
Talampas is one of the old barrios that once lay across the Angat River from Baliuag. Before Bustos had its own parish, families from Talampas, Tanawan and Bonga had to cross the river to reach the church in Baliuag, and it was on one of these crossings in 1862 that a boat carrying children to their baptism capsized. That tragedy led to the founding of the Sto. Niño Parish in 1867.

Today Talampas keeps its own chapel under the parish, dedicated to the Holy Cross. It is run by the barangay's parish pastoral council, which gathers the community for Masses, novenas and the yearly fiesta in honor of the Cross.

value:
Bonga Mayor was one of the two Bonga barrios joined to the new town when Bustos separated from Baliuag in 1867. Its chapel is dedicated to St. Monica, the mother of St. Augustine. The choice reflects the Augustinian roots of the local Church: the Augustinians founded the Sto. Niño Parish of Bustos, and St. Monica and St. Augustine are carved on the main doors of the parish church.

The chapel serves the families of Bonga Mayor and the neighboring part of Tibagan under the Sto. Niño Parish, which holds Masses here and leads the community's devotions and fiesta.

value:
The parish exists because of a tragedy. In 1862 a boat carrying parents, children and godparents to a baptism in Baliuag overturned in the Angat River. The people asked for a parish of their own so no one would have to cross the river again, and chose the Holy Child (Sto. Niño) as patron in memory of the infants who drowned. The Augustinians established the parish in 1867, with Padre Gabriel Alvarez as its first parish priest.

The church has a facade crowned by Christ the Redeemer, with niches for the Sto. Niño, St. Augustine and the crucified Christ. Its wooden doors are carved with St. Monica and St. Augustine, and its ceiling paintings follow the Sistine Chapel. The parish celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2017 together with the town's centennial, and honors the Sto. Niño every third Sunday of January with the Tugyaw (tugtog at sayaw) street dancing.

value:
Minasa are crisp cassava cookies made from cassava flour, egg yolk, yeast, butter and coconut milk. The name comes from the kneading (masa) of the dough. In Spanish times they were baked for well-off Bulakeño families, and local lore links them to the egg yolks left over when egg whites were used in building stone houses. Bustos holds the Minasa Festival every January, and the town's motto is "Minasa ng kaunlaran!"

Zeny's bakes its minasa in small batches. Maria Elena de Lara learned the recipe from her grandmother, who learned it from the family before her. Besides minasa, the store sells lengua de gato, barquillos and other native treats that visitors and balikbayans bring home.

value:

value:
Malamig is a farming barangay south of the town center, on the road toward Liciada and Pandi. Its chapel is dedicated to the Immaculate Conception, a devotion close to Bulacan, whose cathedral in Malolos shares the same title.

The chapel belongs to the Sto. Niño Parish and is cared for by the Malamig parish pastoral council. It is a two-storey cream building with a tall arched entrance, and its blue-and-white interior centers on the crucifix and an image of the Immaculate Conception. The community's biggest celebration is the feast of the Immaculate Conception on 8 December.

value:
Galilee opened on 5 March 2004 in San Pedro, Bustos, as Galilee Mansion and Garden Resort, and has since grown into Galilee Wonderland Waterpark and Hotel. The whole complex is built around biblical themes. Its pools and halls carry names such as Noah's Ark, the Jordan River, Mt. Sinai and the Garden of Eden.

The Wailing Wall follows the Western Wall in Jerusalem, the last remaining wall of the Temple Mount, where pilgrims have long placed written prayers in the cracks. Here visitors can do the same in a quiet corner of the resort, near its church.
